solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Novel about British deposing leader in holy city

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning

indicators.note: deposing means removing from power, and the leader is the first letter, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: Mecca is the holy city of Islam

explanation.surface: A book in which a British figure is overthrown from power in a sacred city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposing leader' drops M from MECCA, leaving ECCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's 1938 book of this title is a famous novel.

clue.text: Society in same old routine to deteriorate

indicators.note: in says the society letter goes inside the routine word

parts.note: a rut is a dull unchanging routine

explanation.surface: High society stuck in the same old routine falls into decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that corrodes goes bad over time, so the verb means to decay or decline.

clue.text: Good man associated with criminal image

parts.note: Ben is a man's name
an e-fit is a computer-made likeness of a suspect

explanation.surface: A decent fellow linked to a picture of a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: An E-FIT is the British police composite face of a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done for your good is an advantage, a noun sense meaning welfare or gain.

clue.text: Credit involves coarse person in illegal scheme

indicators.note: involves means wraps around, takes in the other piece

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
an ape is a clumsy, boorish person

explanation.surface: A credit fraud draws in a vulgar accomplice.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a crime such as a heist or robbery; a dodgy plan.

clue.text: Old man making climb has little desire

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upward, so the word is reversed

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man
petite means small, little

explanation.surface: Dad heads up a mountain but has no great wish to.
explanation.definitionFit: A craving or hunger for something is a desire.

clue.text: Got involved and won prize in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to be medalled is to be awarded a medal, a prize

explanation.surface: An actor who got involved in a show and came away with an award at the try-out.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere in something is to become involved where one is not wanted.

clue.text: People holding hands: one a legendary charmer

indicators.note: holding means containing the other pieces inside

parts.note: men means people
R and L stand for right and left, the two hands
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Folk holding hands, and among them one famous enchanter.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's wizard in legend cast spells, and a charmer is one who casts spells.

clue.text: Policemen, drink consumed, separate and scatter

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, police officers
a sip is a small drink
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Officers finish their drinks, then split up and leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse something is to break it up and spread it away.

clue.text: Loose slate on outbuildings

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters are not fixed in place and can move about

explanation.surface: A slate has come loose on the sheds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheds or shelters propped against a main wall are simple outbuildings.

clue.text: Behaviour left people in debt — billions lost

indicators.note: in says the other pieces go inside
lost means the letter goes missing

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
men means people

explanation.surface: Bad conduct has left people owing money, with billions gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not the past tense of leave here but the nautical side, port.
explanation.definitionFit: One's bearing or conduct, how one carries oneself, is a word for manners.

clue.text: Bird seed gets inside power tool

indicators.note: gets inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a sander is an electric tool for smoothing wood
a pip is a small fruit seed

explanation.surface: A bird's seed gets caught in an electric tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading shorebird of beaches and mudflats is named this.

clue.text: Scoundrel fried seafood, leaving tail

indicators.note: leaving tail means the last letter departs from the word

parts.note: scampi is breaded and fried prawn tails, a pub staple

explanation.surface: A rogue walks off with the fried seafood and leaves only the tail behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or mischievous rogue; a synonym for a villain, usually a lovable one.

clue.text: Maiden one introduced to church leader

parts.note: a maiden voyage or speech is the first one

indicators.note: introduced to means put into the other word

parts.note: a minster is a large church, such as York Minster
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young woman is introduced to the head of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church leader' reads as a bishop, but 'leader' alone is the definition: the title of the head of the Scottish or Welsh government.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a devolved government, e.g. in Scotland, holds this title as its leader.

clue.text: Shot scene with a plot that twists

indicators.note: a plot that twists has its order changed, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A film shot of a scene in a story full of twists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' as in shot silk: shimmering with changing colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot silk shimmers with changing colour, and iridescent milky colours are described the same way.

clue.text: Country-lovers bringing group of three pets round

indicators.note: round means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: pats are affectionate pets with the hand, the verb pet as a noun
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: Some patriotic folk bring three animals along for a walk round.
explanation.definitionFit: People devoted to their nation are patriots, lovers of their country.

clue.text: Landlord's sly look up inside skirts

definitions.note: landlord is, the 's being the verb

indicators.note: skirts means goes around the edge of the other piece

parts.note: inner means inside

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick sly look

explanation.surface: A cheeky landlord takes a sneaky peek up some skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' is a verb meaning goes round, not the garment; 'inside' is a synonym, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or inn keeper is its landlord, the person running a hostelry.

clue.text: Sons in manor surprisingly free with money?

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to secure someone's release by paying

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters land in an unexpected order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: The sons, living in the manor house, are oddly generous with cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here: S joins the letters of MANOR and the whole is rearranged. 'free' is a verb, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay for a captive's release is to buy them out, so it means liberating someone for cash.

clue.text: Person upset by meeting deep disappointment

parts.note: bod is slang for a person

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: low means deep, as of a voice

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed after a meeting that let them down badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch to the torso is a figurative term for a severe setback or let-down.

clue.text: Overdue books waiting to be discovered

parts.note: late means overdue, past its time
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Library books that are overdue lie waiting to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant or hidden, present but not yet showing itself, is undiscovered so far.

clue.text: Old history master understood our group

parts.note: tacit means understood without being said
us means our group

explanation.surface: An old history teacher who was quietly understood by our class.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman historian of the first century wrote the Annals and Histories.

clue.text: Bad one in brawl with Mr Barker

indicators.note: a brawl is a messy fight, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A troublemaker has joined a fight together with a gentleman called Mr Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Barker' looks like one person's name; 'Mr' is fodder and 'Barker' alone is the definition. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A barker is anything that barks, and this German guard-dog breed is one.

clue.text: Wine in varied amounts sent north

indicators.note: sent north says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wine shipped north in assorted quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sent north' reads the letters upward; 'in' marks them as sitting inside 'varied amounts'. The draft lacked the 'in' indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from the Portuguese island in the Atlantic shares its name.

clue.text: Approach news boss declared satisfactory

parts.note: to make a pass is an amorous approach
ED is the editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A reporter's approach to the editor is judged acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam or inspection approved as good enough has been cleared, a past tense.

clue.text: Flyer restricted lines about a term in slammer

parts.note: secret information is restricted to a few
RY is short for railway, a set of lines
bird is slang for time served in prison, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time

explanation.surface: A pilot under tight restrictions, with a few lines about a stint in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' only loosely joins A to RY; the A sits in front of the railway lines rather than inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged African bird of prey known for stamping on snakes is this flyer.

clue.text: Bury Football Club at home in San Siro

definitions.meaning: to bury is to put in a grave

definitions.text: Football Club at home in San Siro
definitions.meaning: ... Milan share the San Siro stadium with AC Milan

explanation.surface: An English town's football club playing at Milan's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like Bury FC, an English club; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay a body in the ground is a verb sense, and the Milan club is the second sense.

clue.text: Certain notes hard to harmonise

parts.note: me (also spelt mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale, so some of them are mes
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Some musical notes are difficult to blend together.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears that engage fit together, and so things that combine well are said to match.

clue.text: European trophies put back in bar

indicators.note: put back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: pots is slang for trophies, cups won in sport

explanation.surface: European cups returned and placed in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to preclude or prevent a party from asserting something, so to block.

clue.text: Patience tried endlessly as oil wasted

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone tried patiently, but the oil was wasted anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TRIED to TRIE; 'wasted' rearranges TRIE with AS OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the British name for card games played alone, which Americans call by this name.

clue.text: Departs before day is over, being stunned

indicators.note: is over says the assembled letters are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
ere is an old word for before
Sat is short for Saturday, a day

explanation.surface: Someone leaves before the day ends, as though knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' reverses D+ERE+SAT, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hit with an electric stun gun is the act described, a passive past-tense verb.

clue.text: Pervert at hotel in course towards conflict

parts.note: to warp is to pervert or distort
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A deviant at a hotel is set on a path to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on this metaphorical route means heading for a fight, from the trail a war party took.
